Check declared resolutions against the commodities they serve

Source: R/check_levels.R
check_model_levels.Rd

The rule interpolate_model() enforces, reported instead of raised. Six classes – demand, supply, import, export, trade, storage – have no aggregation path between a flow and its commodity, so a region or a timeslice declared at a different level than the one the commodity balances at is a cell that is written and never read: the term silently evaluates to zero. Interpolation stops at the first call that finds any; this collects every one, on a model that has not been interpolated yet.

Usage

check_model_levels(object)

Arguments

object

a model or a scenario.

Value

A data.frame with one row per object, commodity and axis, holding the declared and the expected members; no rows when every declaration matches. Printed as a short verdict.

Details

Also reported, which the assertion cannot see from inside interpolation: a commodity naming a @geoframe the model's geoscale does not have, or a @timeframe its calendar does not have.

The coarse direction stays exempt exactly as at interpolation – for a commodity the object only consumes or carries as @aux, and only where the class has an aggregation path.

See also

check_geoscale_regions(), check_feasibility(), aggregate_model_regions()

Other validation: verify_aggregation()

Examples

repo <- newRepository(
  "mini",
  newCommodity("ELC", unit = "MWh"),
  newDemand("DEM", commodity = "ELC",
            demand = data.frame(region = "R1", year = 2020, demand = 10))
)
mod <- newModel("MINI", data = repo, calendar = calendars$annual,
                region = "R1", horizon = horizons$Y2020_2060_by_5)
check_model_levels(mod)
#> Levels: every declaration matches its commodity.
